passages.original: Voti tunc Christianis erat, pro [Veron. eo] Christi nomine gladio percuti [Veron. perpeti]. Verum hostis callidus tarda ad mortem supplicia conquirens animas cupiebat jugulare, non corpora. Et ut ipse, qui ab ipso passus est, Cyprianus ait : Volentibus mori 2, non permitteba- tur occidi. Cujus ut crudelitas notior fiat, duo me- moriae causa exempla subjicimus 3.
passages.english: At that time it was the Christians' prayer to be struck by the sword for the name of Christ. But the cunning enemy, seeking out punishments slow to bring death, desired to slaughter souls, not bodies. And as Cyprian himself, who suffered at his hands, says: those who wished to die were not permitted to be killed. So that his cruelty may become better known, we add two examples for the sake of remembrance.
passages.notes: Bracketed variants from the Verona manuscript are given in the edition: 'eo' for 'pro' (i.e. 'for that name of Christ') and 'perpeti' ('to endure [the sword]') for 'percuti'; the translation follows the main text. Numerals 2 and 3 are footnote marks and have been omitted. The 'enemy' is the devil, as the sentence implies.
